question: Should the repair lane adopt this exact-head fail-closed authorization contract now, including blocking legacy or long-running mutations whenever fresh target, review, covering-PR, required-check, or state-credential proof cannot be established?
rationale: The implementation appears technically sound, but choosing stricter authoritative mutation semantics and accepting the resulting automation pauses is a security and operational policy decision.

options.title: Adopt after exact-head canary
options.body: Run a controlled canary against the current head, reconcile the stale PR-body SHA, and then make this stricter contract the repair default.

options.title: Narrow the rollout
options.body: Enable the guards for selected close or merge phases until operational false-block rates are understood.

options.title: Keep the current contract
options.body: Do not merge if the additional fail-closed pauses are unacceptable for repair availability.

recommendation.title: Adopt after exact-head canary
recommendation.body: Run a controlled canary against the current head, reconcile the stale PR-body SHA, and then make this stricter contract the repair default.
